blocks.text: Consensus lets a group of machines agree on a value — or a sequence of values — even when some of them crash or messages are delayed. Once agreed, the decision never changes. Agreeing on a sequence of commands gives you a **replicated log**, and a replicated log applied in order on every node gives you a **replicated state machine**: a fault-tolerant database, lock service or configuration store.

head: You need consensus for…
Example
rows: Exactly one scheduler / primary at a time
Kubernetes stores all cluster state in etcd
Spanner, CockroachDB, TiKV (Raft per range), Kafka KRaft

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Consensus needs a **majority** (quorum): a cluster of 2f + 1 nodes tolerates f failures. 3 nodes survive 1 failure, 5 survive 2. That's why clusters have odd sizes.

items.title: Terms
items.text: Time is divided into numbered terms; each term has at most one leader.

items.title: Leader election
items.text: Followers that stop hearing heartbeats become candidates, increment the term and request votes; a candidate with a majority becomes leader. Randomised timeouts avoid split votes.

items.title: Log replication
items.text: Clients send commands to the leader, which appends them and replicates to followers; an entry is committed once a majority has stored it.

items.title: Safety
items.text: A node only votes for candidates whose log is at least as up to date as its own, so a new leader always has every committed entry.

blocks.caption: Committing one entry in a 3-node Raft cluster

items: The side with a majority keeps (or elects) a leader and continues to commit.
An old leader on the minority side can't reach a majority, so its writes never commit; when it hears a higher term it steps down.
Clients talking to the minority side get errors or timeouts — consensus systems are **CP**.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Reading from a leader without checking it's still the leader. A deposed leader can serve stale reads. Use read-index / lease reads (etcd linearizable reads) or route reads through the log.

sections.title: Using a coordination service instead of implementing consensus

items: **Leader election:** create an ephemeral key with a lease (etcd) or an ephemeral sequential node (ZooKeeper); the holder of the lowest / existing key is leader.
**Locks with fencing:** etcd returns a revision number with each lease grant — use it as a fencing token.
**Service discovery and config:** watch keys for changes.
Keep data small (KB–MB): coordination services aren't general databases, and every write goes through consensus.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I wouldn't implement consensus; I'd use etcd or ZooKeeper for leader election and store a fencing token so a stale leader's writes are rejected.

items: Every write needs a round trip to a majority: within a region ~1–2 ms; across regions 50–150 ms.
Throughput is bounded by the leader; scale by partitioning into many consensus groups (Raft per range/shard).
Clock-free correctness, but **leases** (for fast reads) do assume bounded clock drift.
